chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said:
I asked him about the person in ihram riding in the qubbah (a covered saddle/backpack), so he said, 'No.' I said, 'And the woman in ihram?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.اَلْقُبَّةَ: A covered saddle or structure used for riding, often implying a specific type of shelter or seat
key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمَةُ: The woman in the state of ihram
key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (sacred consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in ruling for men and women regarding riding in a qubbah while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Tusi’s Tahdhib, clarifies the specific prohibition of 'qubbah' (a covered saddle or structure) for men in ihram, distinguishing it from the general prohibition of covering the head. Women are permitted to use it due to their need for protection from the sun and elements, reflecting the juristic principle of accommodating women's physical needs during pilgrimage rituals.
